    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "decisions/gates.yaml",
        "provenance.yaml",
        "scripts/ci_gates.py",
        "scripts/harness.py",
        "scripts/kit/manifest.yaml"
      ]
    },
    "938ebd8c7443e4132b84d4ff967e9bb7af788ba4": {

      "author_utc": "2026-10-14T21:42:35Z",
      "body": "Three runner attempts (two GLM Flash, one Sonnet 5.5) left the tree red; the\norchestrating session completed it: the AGENTS.md rule names \"every question\",\nand the question-context adoption day is the earliest merge day, 2026-10-15\n(plan step 5), so the 2026-10-14 interview answers stay exempt (Q-5).\nmake verify green.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HoLR7RKVm2BmkNJPjEVdDq\n",

    "fa3f30c019ce23e0958c91c3ebe094695e992f50": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-10T10:51:23Z",
      "body": "Amends point 9 of ADR 0020. The maintainer answered the decision block of\nthe swarm-report-format spec on 2026-11-10 with option 1: a topic report\nthat fails its format contract may be corrected once by the model that\nwrote it. That adds at most 33 + 3N calls to the 39 + 3N of a run. No other\nretry is allowed; the time limits stay.\n\nThe runner still enforces 39 + 3N; the code follows in the change\nswarm-report-format.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Jh36RJDeJ5FJBMMendzXmJ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "fa3f30c019ce23e0958c91c3ebe094695e992f50",
      "subject": "decide(research-swarm): one correction call per topic report raises the ceiling to 72 + 6N (bead coding-harness-4q9y)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "docs/adr/0020-phase-1-research-swarm.md"
      ]
    },
    "fe1ad6578816f505562ed3c055e6e819c809c995": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-08T12:26:48Z",
      "body": "Runner format before `make verify` (ruff check --fix with safe fixes only, then ruff format):\n- Attempt 1 (codex): ruff changed no file.\n",

      "hash": "fe1ad6578816f505562ed3c055e6e819c809c995",
      "subject": "fix(archive-closed-changes): repair taken findings R-2",

    "fe864e5906beaa78521f08884dd5714f2835674e": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-25T18:28:20Z",
      "body": "Deep review RS-3-2 (BLOCKER): the repository seats' path lock judged a\nfile:// URL as a name inside the worktree while Pi reads the real path,\nso any file on the machine reached a Go model. The lock now mirrors Pi's\nnormalizePath (unicode spaces, @, ~ refused, file:// through\nfileURLToPath) before it confines, and for read also every fallback name\nPi's resolveReadPath tries (RS-3-6). Re-checked on the pinned Pi 1.2.0\nunder Node 22.\n\nDeep review RS-1-2 (BLOCKER): the research-handoff gate split research.md\nwith str.splitlines, which breaks at U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 that the runner\nkeeps raw in JSON strings; a complete run became not measured. The gate\nnow breaks lines at LF, CRLF and CR only.\n\nRS-1-9: a run envelope's markers are hard boundaries that end a foreign\nMarkdown fence left open by earlier prose. RS-1-3: under later non-criteria\nsections only criterion-shaped numbered items count as criteria.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "fe864e5906beaa78521f08884dd5714f2835674e",
      "subject": "fix(research-swarm): path lock follows Pi's path rules; handoff gate reads lines as JSON does",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/check_research_handoff.py",
        "tests/test_research_handoff.py"
      ]
    },
    "fee253ded66d6c15cb211958a970a71ad5db4f75": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-20T11:31:00Z",

      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "fee253ded66d6c15cb211958a970a71ad5db4f75",

          "end_line": 166,
          "excerpt": "def read_updated(text: str) -> str | date:\n    \"\"\"The `updated:` date of a header, or the reason there is none.\"\"\"\n    m = _BLOCK.match(text)\n    if not m:\n        return NO_FRONTMATTER\n    zeilen = [z for z in m.group(1).split(\"\\n\") if _UPDATED_LINE.match(z)]  # CRLF: each keeps its `\\r`\n    if not zeilen:\n        return MISSING\n    if len(zeilen) > 1:\n        return DUPLICATE\n    wert = _VALUE.match(zeilen[0][len(\"updated:\") :].strip())\n    if not wert:\n        return UNREADABLE\n    try:\n        return date.fromisoformat(wert.group(1))\n    except ValueError:\n        return UNREADABLE\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py",
          "reference": "read_updated",
          "start_line": 150,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py::stamped",
          "end_line": 247,
          "excerpt": "def stamped(text: str, today: date) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The text with its header's `updated:` set to today, by editing one line; unchanged without a header.\n\n    The pure half of ``stamp``: a writer that must replace a file in one atomic step (the research append,\n    deep review RS-2-6) stamps the bytes it is about to write instead of rewriting the file a second time.\n    \"\"\"\n    m = _BLOCK.match(text)\n    if not m:\n        return text\n    zeilen = m.group(1).split(\"\\n\")\n    neu = f\"updated: {today.isoformat()}\"\n    vorhanden = [i for i, z in enumerate(zeilen) if _UPDATED_LINE.match(z)]\n    if len(vorhanden) > 1:\n        return text\n    if vorhanden:\n        # A CRLF line keeps its `\\r`; the value and anything after it are replaced.\n        zeilen[vorhanden[0]] = neu + (\"\\r\" if zeilen[vorhanden[0]].endswith(\"\\r\") else \"\")\n    else:\n        nach = [i for i, z in enumerate(zeilen) if z.startswith(\"last_reviewed:\")]\n        stelle = nach[0] if nach else len(zeilen) - 1\n        zeilen.insert(stelle + 1, neu + (\"\\r\" if zeilen[stelle].endswith(\"\\r\") else \"\"))\n    return text[: m.start(1)] + \"\\n\".join(zeilen) + text[m.end(1) :]\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py",
          "reference": "stamped",
          "start_line": 226,

          "end_line": 135,
          "excerpt": "def is_held(rel: str, paths: list[dict[str, Any]], excluded: list[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: a Markdown file, not excluded, whose longest prefix says `required`.\"\"\"\n    if not rel.endswith(\".md\"):\n        return False\n    if any(rel.startswith(e) for e in excluded):\n        return False\n    treffer = [p for p in paths if rel.startswith(str(p.get(\"prefix\", \"\")))]\n    if not treffer:\n        return False\n    laengster = max(treffer, key=lambda p: len(str(p[\"prefix\"])))\n    return laengster.get(\"frontmatter\") == \"required\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_ledger_is_cleared_before_the_documents_are_stamped(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    # Pre-review row P239-2 (2026-10-25). Planted fault: the marker is cleared after `prepare_derived`, so the\n    # plan's `updated:` stamp misses the runner's own edit and the frontmatter-current gate goes red.\n    world.plan.write_text(\n        \"---\\ntitle: Plan\\nupdated: 2026-09-30\\nbead: demo-1\\n---\\n\\n# Plan\\n\\n## Criterion ledger\\n\\n\"\n        \"- 1: not yet written tests/test_new.py::test_new — the attempt writes it\\n\\n## Time used\\n\",\n        encoding=\"utf-8\",\n    )\n    git(world.root, \"add\", \"-A\")\n    git(world.root, \"commit\", \"--quiet\", \"-m\", \"ledger with a marker\")\n    seen: list[str] = []\n    real = stage2.prepare_derived\n\n    def watching(*args, **kwargs):\n        seen.append(world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        return real(*args, **kwargs)\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"prepare_derived\", watching)\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"implemented\",\n                \"plant\": {\"tests/test_new.py\": \"def test_new():\\n    pass\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            }\n        ],\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 0\n    assert seen and \"not yet written\" not in seen[0], \"the documents were stamped before the ledger was cleared\"\n",

A part postponed rather than refused says what brings\nit back.\n\nA `feature` without a `design.md` says here, in one sentence, why it does\nwithout the design phase 2b (`prompts/02b-design.md`).\n\n## Protected areas\n\nThe paths or areas this change must not touch, each with its reason.           "excerpt": "class Verdict:\n    \"\"\"Collects findings and computes an exit code from them.\"\"\"\n\n    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    def add(\n        self,\n        level: Level,\n        message: str,\n        detail: str = \"\",\n        ramp: Ramp | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self.findings.append(Finding(level, message, detail, ramp))\n\n    def info(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\") -> None:\n        self.add(Level.INFO, message, detail)\n\n    def drift(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\", ramp: Ramp | None = None) -> None:\n        self.add(Level.DRIFT, message, detail, ramp)\n\n    def block(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\", ramp: Ramp | None = None) -> None:\n        self.add(Level.BLOCK, message, detail, ramp)\n\n    def at(self, level: Level) -> list[Finding]:\n        return [f for f in self.findings if f.effective_level() == level]\n\n    def exit_code(self, strict: bool = False) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Highest level reached. Without `--strict` DRIFT does not block.\n\n        The reason is stated above: the other side of a DRIFT finding moves\n        without a commit in this repo. At somebody else's pull request that would\n        be noise; in a scheduled run (`--strict`) it is the signal.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.findings:\n            return 0\n        worst = max(f.effective_level() for f in self.findings)\n        if worst == Level.DRIFT and not strict:\n            return 0\n        return int(worst)\n\n    def render(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Report in reading order: first what blocks, then what merely stands out.\"\"\"\n        if not self.findings:\n            return \"OK — no deviation.\"\n        out: list[str] = []\n        for level in (Level.BLOCK, Level.DRIFT, Level.INFO):\n            group = self.at(level)\n            if not group:\n                continue\n            out.append(f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[level]} ({len(group)}):\")\n            for f in group:\n                out.append(f\"  - {f.message}\")\n                if f.detail:\n                    out.extend(f\"      {line}\" for line in f.detail.splitlines())\n                if f.ramp is not None and not f.ramp.due:\n                    out.append(\n                        f\"      [valve {f.ramp.name}] reported as \"\n                        f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[f.ramp.until_then].strip()} instead of \"\n                        f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[f.ramp.target].strip()}, until: {f.ramp.condition}\"\n                    )\n            out.append(\"\")\n        blocks = self.at(Level.BLOCK)\n        if blocks and len(blocks) < len(self.findings):\n            # Readers that keep only the tail (the stage-2 runner's diagnostics) lose the top of a long\n            # report; the blocking messages stand last as well (bead coding-harness-2g7y).\n            out.append(f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[Level.BLOCK]} ({len(blocks)}), repeated last:\")\n            out.extend(f\"  - {f.message}\" for f in blocks)\n        return \"\\n\".join(out).rstrip()\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_frontmatter(text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse registry metadata from text, including YAML merge keys and aliases.\"\"\"\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\\n\"):\n        return None\n    end = text.find(\"\\n---\", 4)\n    if end == -1:\n        return None\n    try:\n        loaded = yaml.safe_load(text[4:end])\n    except yaml.YAMLError:\n        return None\n    return loaded if isinstance(loaded, dict) else None\n",

          "excerpt": "class Verdict:\n    \"\"\"Collects findings and computes an exit code from them.\"\"\"\n\n    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    def add(\n        self,\n        level: Level,\n        message: str,\n        detail: str = \"\",\n        ramp: Ramp | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self.findings.append(Finding(level, message, detail, ramp))\n\n    def info(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\") -> None:\n        self.add(Level.INFO, message, detail)\n\n    def drift(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\", ramp: Ramp | None = None) -> None:\n        self.add(Level.DRIFT, message, detail, ramp)\n\n    def block(self, message: str, detail: str = \"\", ramp: Ramp | None = None) -> None:\n        self.add(Level.BLOCK, message, detail, ramp)\n\n    def at(self, level: Level) -> list[Finding]:\n        return [f for f in self.findings if f.effective_level() == level]\n\n    def exit_code(self, strict: bool = False) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Highest level reached. Without `--strict` DRIFT does not block.\n\n        The reason is stated above: the other side of a DRIFT finding moves\n        without a commit in this repo. At somebody else's pull request that would\n        be noise; in a scheduled run (`--strict`) it is the signal.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.findings:\n            return 0\n        worst = max(f.effective_level() for f in self.findings)\n        if worst == Level.DRIFT and not strict:\n            return 0\n        return int(worst)\n\n    def render(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Report in reading order: first what blocks, then what merely stands out.\"\"\"\n        if not self.findings:\n            return \"OK — no deviation.\"\n        out: list[str] = []\n        for level in (Level.BLOCK, Level.DRIFT, Level.INFO):\n            group = self.at(level)\n            if not group:\n                continue\n            out.append(f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[level]} ({len(group)}):\")\n            for f in group:\n                out.append(f\"  - {f.message}\")\n                if f.detail:\n                    out.extend(f\"      {line}\" for line in f.detail.splitlines())\n                if f.ramp is not None and not f.ramp.due:\n                    out.append(\n                        f\"      [valve {f.ramp.name}] reported as \"\n                        f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[f.ramp.until_then].strip()} instead of \"\n                        f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[f.ramp.target].strip()}, until: {f.ramp.condition}\"\n                    )\n            out.append(\"\")\n        blocks = self.at(Level.BLOCK)\n        if blocks and len(blocks) < len(self.findings):\n            # Readers that keep only the tail (the stage-2 runner's diagnostics) lose the top of a long\n            # report; the blocking messages stand last as well (bead coding-harness-2g7y).\n            out.append(f\"{LEVEL_LABEL[Level.BLOCK]} ({len(blocks)}), repeated last:\")\n            out.extend(f\"  - {f.message}\" for f in blocks)\n        return \"\\n\".join(out).rstrip()\n",

          "excerpt": "def load_map(root: Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"`paths:` and `excluded:` of the provenance map, or CannotMeasure.\"\"\"\n    karte = root / \"provenance.yaml\"\n    try:\n        doc = yaml.safe_load(karte.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"cannot read {karte}: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or not isinstance(doc.get(\"paths\"), list):\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"{karte} has no `paths:` list\")\n    excluded = doc.get(\"excluded\") or []\n    if not isinstance(excluded, list):\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"{karte}: `excluded:` is not a list\")\n    return doc[\"paths\"], [str(e) for e in excluded]\n",

          "excerpt": "def answering_role(root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 10: the `owner_role` of the map's entry for `decisions/answers/`, declared under `roles:`.\"\"\"\n    path, where = provenance_map(root)\n    try:\n        doc = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (OSError, ValueError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:\n        raise Refused(f\"cannot read {where} ({exc}); it must name who answers, under `paths:`:\\n{OWNER_ENTRY}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(doc, dict):\n        raise Refused(f\"{where} is not a mapping; add under `paths:`:\\n{OWNER_ENTRY}\")\n    listed = doc.get(\"paths\")\n    if not isinstance(listed, list):\n        listed = []\n    entries = [e for e in listed if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"prefix\") == ANSWERS_PREFIX]\n    if not entries:\n        raise Refused(f'{where} has no `paths:` entry with prefix \"{ANSWERS_PREFIX}\"; add:\\n{OWNER_ENTRY}')\n    role = entries[0].get(\"owner_role\")\n    if not isinstance(role, str) or not role.strip():\n        raise Refused(\n            f'the `paths:` entry for \"{ANSWERS_PREFIX}\" in {where} has no `owner_role:`; '\n            \"add `owner_role: <a role declared under roles:>` to it\"\n        )\n    roles = doc.get(\"roles\")\n    if not isinstance(roles, dict) or role not in roles:\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"`owner_role: {role}` in {where} names no role under `roles:`; \"\n            f\"add `{role}:` under `roles:`, or name a role that is there\"\n        )\n    return role\n",

          "excerpt": "def committed_decided_prefixes(root: Path, code: str = \"HEAD\") -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Prefixes the committed provenance map reserves to human decisions.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load(git_out(root, \"show\", f\"{code}:provenance.yaml\"))\n    except yaml.YAMLError as error:\n        raise Failed(f\"the committed provenance.yaml cannot be read ({error})\") from error\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        raise Failed(\"the committed provenance.yaml is not a mapping\")\n    entries = data.get(\"paths\")\n    if entries is None:\n        return []\n    if not isinstance(entries, list):\n        raise Failed(\"the committed provenance.yaml has no readable paths list\")\n    decided: list[str] = []\n    for entry in entries:\n        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not isinstance(entry.get(\"prefix\"), str):\n            raise Failed(\"the committed provenance.yaml has an entry without a string prefix\")\n        allowed = entry.get(\"allowed\")\n        if isinstance(allowed, list) and allowed and set(allowed) == {\"human-decided\"}:\n            decided.append(entry[\"prefix\"])\n    return decided\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_frontmatter(text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse registry metadata from text, including YAML merge keys and aliases.\"\"\"\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\\n\"):\n        return None\n    end = text.find(\"\\n---\", 4)\n    if end == -1:\n        return None\n    try:\n        loaded = yaml.safe_load(text[4:end])\n    except yaml.YAMLError:\n        return None\n    return loaded if isinstance(loaded, dict) else None\n",

        {
          "citation": "scripts/handover_schema.py::frontmatter",
          "end_line": 142,
          "excerpt": "def frontmatter(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Reads the flat keys of the frontmatter.\n\n    Nested blocks (`review:`, `produced_by:`) are taken with their prefix —\n    `review.status` instead of `status`. Without this separation the review\n    status would overwrite the handover status, and both are called `status`.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\\n\"):\n        return {}\n    block = text.split(\"---\\n\", 2)[1]\n    felder: dict[str, str] = {}\n    eltern = None\n    for zeile in block.splitlines():\n        if not zeile.strip() or zeile.lstrip().startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        eingerueckt = zeile.startswith((\" \", \"\\t\"))\n        schluessel, _, wert = zeile.strip().partition(\":\")\n        wert = wert.strip().strip('\"')\n        if eingerueckt and eltern:\n            felder[f\"{eltern}.{schluessel.strip()}\"] = wert\n        else:\n            eltern = schluessel.strip() if not wert else None\n            felder[schluessel.strip()] = wert\n    return felder\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/handover_schema.py",
          "reference": "frontmatter",
          "start_line": 119,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::frontmatter_fields",
          "end_line": 9114,
          "excerpt": "def frontmatter_fields(text: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:\n    \"\"\"Effective protected values, using the registry's parser (and its merge semantics).\"\"\"\n    # Path.read_text in the registry uses universal newlines. Match it for byte snapshots.\n    try:\n        values = plans_registry.parse_frontmatter(text.replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\").replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\"))\n    except (ValueError, OverflowError, RecursionError):\n        # SafeLoader constructors can reject values (such as invalid dates) without a YAMLError.\n        return None\n    if values is None:\n        return None\n    return {key: values[key] for key in LIFECYCLE_FIELDS if key in values}\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",

      "statement": "There is no shared front-matter reader: at least five modules parse the document header with different acceptance. `check_adr_answers._BLOCK` and `check_interview_minimums._BLOCK` are byte-identical and tolerate a BOM plus CRLF with a closing `---` line; `check_frontmatter_current._BLOCK` tolerates BOM and CRLF but anchors on `\\n---\\r?\\n`; `check_research_currency._BLOCK` is near-identical to the latter; `plans_registry.parse_frontmatter` requires the text to start with exactly `---\\n` and returns None otherwise; `handover_schema.frontmatter` does the same; `stage2.frontmatter_fields` delegates to `plans_registry.parse_frontmatter` after normalising CRLF. A plan artefact with a BOM or CRLF header is therefore held by one gate and reported as unreadable by another."

          "excerpt": "def _frontmatter_template(name: str, bead: str, owner: str, heute: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Frontmatter with every field from `plans_registry.REQUIRED` filled in.\n\n    Order and extra fields follow `plans/_README.md` — `supersedes` and\n    `superseded_by` are the only two fields that may be `null`.\n\n    `provenance: human-written` and **no** `produced_by` block: this file was\n    written by a deterministic call that a human issued. It used to say\n    `ai-drafted-reviewed` with\n    `produced_by: {kind: llm-session, name: unknown}` — a provenance that\n    nobody had at the time of writing, and that the provenance gate cannot\n    refute, because `plans/` permits exactly the two classes `human-written`\n    and `ai-drafted-reviewed`. Whoever fills the body with a language model\n    brings both up to date; the generated text says so.\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"\"\"---\ntitle: \"Research — {name}\"\nstatus: draft\nimplementation_status: none\ndate: {heute}\nlast_reviewed: {heute}\nupdated: {heute}\nsupersedes: null\nsuperseded_by: null\nbead: {bead}\nowner: {owner}\nprovenance: human-written\ntags: [research]\n---\n\n\"\"\"\n",

Whoever fills it\n> with a language model sets `ai-drafted-reviewed` and adds `produced_by:` and\n> `review:` (`provenance.yaml`, class `ai-drafted-reviewed`,\n> `review_required: true`).\n\"\"\"\n",

          "citation": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py::stamped",
          "end_line": 247,
          "excerpt": "def stamped(text: str, today: date) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The text with its header's `updated:` set to today, by editing one line; unchanged without a header.\n\n    The pure half of ``stamp``: a writer that must replace a file in one atomic step (the research append,\n    deep review RS-2-6) stamps the bytes it is about to write instead of rewriting the file a second time.\n    \"\"\"\n    m = _BLOCK.match(text)\n    if not m:\n        return text\n    zeilen = m.group(1).split(\"\\n\")\n    neu = f\"updated: {today.isoformat()}\"\n    vorhanden = [i for i, z in enumerate(zeilen) if _UPDATED_LINE.match(z)]\n    if len(vorhanden) > 1:\n        return text\n    if vorhanden:\n        # A CRLF line keeps its `\\r`; the value and anything after it are replaced.\n        zeilen[vorhanden[0]] = neu + (\"\\r\" if zeilen[vorhanden[0]].endswith(\"\\r\") else \"\")\n    else:\n        nach = [i for i, z in enumerate(zeilen) if z.startswith(\"last_reviewed:\")]\n        stelle = nach[0] if nach else len(zeilen) - 1\n        zeilen.insert(stelle + 1, neu + (\"\\r\" if zeilen[stelle].endswith(\"\\r\") else \"\"))\n    return text[: m.start(1)] + \"\\n\".join(zeilen) + text[m.end(1) :]\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py",
          "reference": "stamped",
          "start_line": 226,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false

requires an existing bead, creates none |\n| Hygiene | `scripts/plans_registry.py` | `--check` reports, `--index` writes `plans/INDEX.md` |\n| Sub-agents | `.claude/agents/explorer.md`, `reviewer.md` | read-only, model pinned |\n| Stop hook | `.claude/hooks/session-stop/check-tests-green.sh` | blocks the end of a turn on a red tree |\n| Enforcement | `decisions/gates.yaml` | **the one gate list** (D-10); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is generated from it |\n| Decisions | `scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, `scripts/harness.py`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` | the gate `adr-answers`; `decide adr` records the maintainer's ADR answers; the decision pull request's block |\n| Interview | `scripts/check_interview_minimums.py` | the gate `interview-minimums`: counts counted interview records per class at the spec gate and in verify, sees ADR paths in every diff state, compares per context — first parent on the main line (a `main` checkout or the hosted main-line run), else the merge base; a detached HEAD at `origin/main` is not measured and exits 3 — attributes an ADR edit to the change that claims it under `adr_files` (ADR 0014) — subject after the adoption day of `decisions/adoption.yaml`, here 2026-10-08 |\n| Question context | `scripts/check_question_context.py` | the gate `question-context`: every `status: answered` record recorded on or after the adoption day keeps the context that was shown with it in its own `context` field — presence only, in live and archived `decisions.md`, with or without a spec; the cut-off is each answer's own recording day, read from the one em-dash date (`— YYYY-MM-DD`) that ends its decision statement (a closing parenthetical remark may follow); the adoption day itself is subject, older answers stay exempt, unreadable evidence exits 3 (ADR 0018) |\n| Criterion tests | `scripts/check_criterion_ledger.py` | the gate `criterion-ledger`: every test a plan's `## Criterion ledger` names is defined, every criterion of the spec has an entry, a not-yet-written entry stands only while the change is live;           "excerpt": "def load_map(root: Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"`paths:` and `excluded:` of the provenance map, or CannotMeasure.\"\"\"\n    karte = root / \"provenance.yaml\"\n    try:\n        doc = yaml.safe_load(karte.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"cannot read {karte}: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or not isinstance(doc.get(\"paths\"), list):\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"{karte} has no `paths:` list\")\n    excluded = doc.get(\"excluded\") or []\n    if not isinstance(excluded, list):\n        raise CannotMeasure(f\"{karte}: `excluded:` is not a list\")\n    return doc[\"paths\"], [str(e) for e in excluded]\n",

          "end_line": 135,
          "excerpt": "def is_held(rel: str, paths: list[dict[str, Any]], excluded: list[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: a Markdown file, not excluded, whose longest prefix says `required`.\"\"\"\n    if not rel.endswith(\".md\"):\n        return False\n    if any(rel.startswith(e) for e in excluded):\n        return False\n    treffer = [p for p in paths if rel.startswith(str(p.get(\"prefix\", \"\")))]\n    if not treffer:\n        return False\n    laengster = max(treffer, key=lambda p: len(str(p[\"prefix\"])))\n    return laengster.get(\"frontmatter\") == \"required\"\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "reference": "is_held",

          "end_line": 166,
          "excerpt": "def read_updated(text: str) -> str | date:\n    \"\"\"The `updated:` date of a header, or the reason there is none.\"\"\"\n    m = _BLOCK.match(text)\n    if not m:\n        return NO_FRONTMATTER\n    zeilen = [z for z in m.group(1).split(\"\\n\") if _UPDATED_LINE.match(z)]  # CRLF: each keeps its `\\r`\n    if not zeilen:\n        return MISSING\n    if len(zeilen) > 1:\n        return DUPLICATE\n    wert = _VALUE.match(zeilen[0][len(\"updated:\") :].strip())\n    if not wert:\n        return UNREADABLE\n    try:\n        return date.fromisoformat(wert.group(1))\n    except ValueError:\n        return UNREADABLE\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py",
          "reference": "read_updated",

          "excerpt": "def findings(root: Path, today: date, utc_today: date) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"(path, kind, detail) for every held file that is reported. Empty = green.\"\"\"\n    files = held_files(root)\n    if not files:\n        # A gate over an empty set cannot bite, and green here would say it did.\n        raise CannotMeasure(\n            \"provenance.yaml holds no document: no `frontmatter: required` prefix matches a Markdown file, \"\n            \"so the check measures nothing\"\n        )\n    refs = reference_dates(root, files, today)\n    grenze = utc_today + timedelta(days=1)\n    befunde: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    for f in files:\n        gelesen = read_updated((root / f).read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"))\n        if isinstance(gelesen, str):\n            befunde.append((f, gelesen, \"\"))\n            continue\n        ref, woher = refs[f]\n        if gelesen < ref:\n            befunde.append((f, STALE, f\"updated {gelesen} is older than its last change {ref} ({woher})\"))\n        elif gelesen > grenze:\n            befunde.append((f, FUTURE, f\"updated {gelesen} is later than tomorrow (UTC) {grenze}\"))\n    return befunde\n",

          "excerpt": "def adopted_on(root: Path, gate: str) -> date:\n    \"\"\"The day `root` adopted `gate`, or NotRecorded.\"\"\"\n    path = root / RECORD\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} does not exist — {_remedy(gate)}\") from None\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} cannot be read ({exc}) — {_remedy(gate)}\") from None\n    try:\n        data = check_adr_answers.strict_load(text)\n    except (yaml.YAMLError, ValueError) as exc:  # ValueError: an impossible date such as 2026-02-30\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} is not valid YAML ({' '.join(str(exc).split())}) — {_remedy(gate)}\") from None\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} is not a YAML mapping — {_remedy(gate)}\")\n    version = data.get(\"schema_version\")\n    if not (type(version) is int and version == 1):\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} lacks `schema_version: 1` (it holds {version!r}) — {_remedy(gate)}\")\n    adopted = data.get(\"adopted\")\n    if not isinstance(adopted, dict):\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} has no `adopted:` mapping — {_remedy(gate)}\")\n    if gate not in adopted:\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} holds no day for {gate} — {_remedy(gate)}\")\n    day = adopted[gate]\n    if type(day) is not date:\n        raise NotRecorded(f\"{RECORD} holds {day!r} for {gate}, which is no unquoted date — {_remedy(gate)}\")\n    return day\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def _frontmatter_template(name: str, bead: str, owner: str, heute: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Frontmatter with every field from `plans_registry.REQUIRED` filled in.\n\n    Order and extra fields follow `plans/_README.md` — `supersedes` and\n    `superseded_by` are the only two fields that may be `null`.\n\n    `provenance: human-written` and **no** `produced_by` block: this file was\n    written by a deterministic call that a human issued. It used to say\n    `ai-drafted-reviewed` with\n    `produced_by: {kind: llm-session, name: unknown}` — a provenance that\n    nobody had at the time of writing, and that the provenance gate cannot\n    refute, because `plans/` permits exactly the two classes `human-written`\n    and `ai-drafted-reviewed`. Whoever fills the body with a language model\n    brings both up to date; the generated text says so.\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"\"\"---\ntitle: \"Research — {name}\"\nstatus: draft\nimplementation_status: none\ndate: {heute}\nlast_reviewed: {heute}\nupdated: {heute}\nsupersedes: null\nsuperseded_by: null\nbead: {bead}\nowner: {owner}\nprovenance: human-written\ntags: [research]\n---\n\n\"\"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_new_change_creates_the_folder_and_a_current_index(workflow, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Acceptance of cke, first half: the entry scaffolds here.\n\n    The scaffold's stamp date is pinned: a `date` subclass overriding only\n    `today()` sits on the shared `datetime` module (`new_change.dt`), and the\n    assertion reads the pinned value directly — this module's\n    `from datetime import date` is import-bound and would keep reading the\n    calendar clock after the write.\n    \"\"\"\n    day = date(2026, 11, 10)\n\n    class PinnedDate(date):\n        @classmethod\n        def today(cls) -> date:\n            return day\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(new_change.dt, \"date\", PinnedDate)\n    exit_code = new_change.main([\"probe\", \"--bead\", OPEN_BEAD])\n    assert exit_code == 0\n    assert (workflow / \"changes\" / \"probe\" / \"research.md\").is_file()\n    assert reg.INDEX.is_file(), \"the index was not rendered along\"\n    # qd7: a new document is born current, or the check behind `frontmatter-current` would report it.\n    scaffold = (workflow / \"changes\" / \"probe\" / \"research.md\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert f\"\\nupdated: {day.isoformat()}\\n\" in scaffold.split(\"\\n---\\n\", 1)[0] + \"\\n\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def run(basis: Path, export: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Prueft alle Zitationen unter `basis` gegen den Export.\"\"\"\n    bekannt = _bekannte_ids(export)\n    if not bekannt:\n        return [f\"der Export {export} nennt keine einzige ID — die Pruefung misst nichts\"]\n    befunde: list[str] = []\n    dateien = sorted(basis.rglob(\"*.md\"))\n    for p in dateien:\n        rel = p.relative_to(basis)\n        text = p.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        for treffer in MUSTER.finditer(text):\n            voll = PRAEFIX + treffer.group(1)\n            if voll not in bekannt:\n                befunde.append(f\"{rel}: haengende ID {voll} — im Export nicht bekannt\")\n    return befunde\n",

          "citation": "scripts/check_decision_continuity.py::run",
          "end_line": 88,
          "excerpt": "def run(target: Path, adr_dir: Path = ADR_DIR) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Checks continuity and ADR coverage. Returns findings; empty = green.\"\"\"\n    befunde: list[str] = []\n    if not target.is_file():\n        return [f\"Target file missing: {target}\"]\n    text = target.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    stueck = re.split(r\"^## Decision continuity\\s*$\", text, maxsplit=1, flags=re.M)\n    if len(stueck) < 2:\n        return [f\"{target.name}: no 'Decision continuity' section\"]\n    tabelle = stueck[1].split(\"\\n## \", 1)[0]\n\n    for sid in (*EXPECTED_D, *EXPECTED_O):\n        if not re.search(rf\"\\b{re.escape(sid)}\\b\", tabelle):\n            befunde.append(f\"{target.name}: Decision {sid} missing from the continuity table\")\n\n    for schluessel, adrs in AMENDMENT_ADRS.items():\n        for adr in adrs:\n            pfad = adr_dir / adr\n            if not pfad.is_file():\n                befunde.append(f\"ADR missing: docs/adr/{adr} (for {schluessel})\")\n                continue\n            inhalt = pfad.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            zitieren = [s for s in (schluessel,) if s.startswith((\"D-\", \"O-\"))] + (\n                [\"coordinator\"] if schluessel == \"coordinator-permission\" else []\n            )\n            for z in zitieren:\n                if not re.search(rf\"\\b{re.escape(z)}\\b\", inhalt):\n                    befunde.append(f\"docs/adr/{adr}: does not name '{z}' — the mapping is empty\")\n    return befunde\n",

          "end_line": 1016,
          "excerpt": "def run(root: Path, only: str | None, out=print) -> int:\n    findings: list[str] = []\n    pending: list[str] = []\n    unmeasured: list[str] = []\n    try:\n        folders = changes(root, only)\n    except CannotMeasure as error:\n        out(f\"research-handoff: not measured - {error}\")\n        return 3\n    for label, folder in folders:\n        try:\n            outcome = check_change(folder, label)\n        except CannotMeasure as error:\n            unmeasured.append(str(error))\n            continue\n        findings += outcome.findings\n        pending += outcome.pending\n        for note in outcome.notes:\n            out(note)\n    for line in pending:\n        out(line)\n    if unmeasured:\n        for line in unmeasured:\n            out(f\"research-handoff: not measured - {line}\")\n        return 3\n    for line in findings:\n        out(f\"research-handoff: {line}\")\n    if findings:\n        out(f\"research-handoff: {len(findings)} finding(s)\")\n        return 1\n    out(f\"research-handoff: measured {len(folders)} change(s), nothing found\")\n    return 0\n",

after a research swarm every obligation item answered and linked (`research_items`, `research_neighbours`; minimums are no ceiling) | [`01a-interview.md`](../prompts/01a-interview.md) |\n| 2 | Spec | `plans/changes/<name>/spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]`; after a research swarm `neighbours:` and every criterion's `*Basis:*` match the research (`research-handoff`) | [`02-spec.md`](../prompts/02-spec.md) |\n| 2a | Spec review | rows for `findings.md`, dimension `SPEC`; then the revised `spec.md` | every row worked into the spec or rejected with a reason; no open `[AMBIGUITY]` | [`02a-spec-review.md`](../prompts/02a-spec-review.md) |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `plans/changes/<name>/design.md` | validator green; for an `architectural` change, an ADR draft in it | [`02b-design.md`](../prompts/02b-design.md) |\n| 3 | Plan | `plans/changes/<name>/plan.md` | validator green | [`03-plan.md`](../prompts/03-plan.md) |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green | [`04-implement.md`](../prompts/04-implement.md) |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | the loop rows — outside the repository until the phase-6 verdict, then in `findings.md` (`release-loop`) | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 | [`04b-review-loop.md`](../prompts/04b-review-loop.md) |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | the stop hook blocks on a red tree | [`05-verify.md`](../prompts/05-verify.md) |\n| 6 | Review | `plans/changes/<name>/findings.md` | the branch has merged `main` before the review, and the verdict holds only for the commit it saw (§3, \"Pull requests stay mergeable\"); no open `[AMBIGUITY]`, no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as a BLOCKER | [`06-review.md`](../prompts/06-review.md) |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green | [`07-commit.md`](../prompts/07-commit.md) |\n\nPhase 1a is **owed where a minimum stands** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a\n`feature` owes at least three distinct, substantive questions the maintainer\nanswered; creating or changing an ADR owes five, whatever the class — a\nfeature that also carries an ADR owes five in total, never the sum; a `spike`\nowes the three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change owes one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. The gate `interview-minimums`\n(`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) counts the records at the spec gate\nand in `make verify`: only distinct, maintainer-answered records count, an\nagent's answer, an open question and a repeated confirmation count for\nnothing, and the check sees ADR paths in every diff state — committed,\nstaged, unstaged, untracked. The duty is prospective: a change is subject\nwhen its spec `date` is later than the repository's adoption day, which\n`decisions/adoption.yaml` records per repository and `scripts/adoption.py`\nreads — here **2026-10-08**, the merge date of the change that introduced the\nrule.           "end_line": 131,
          "excerpt": "# ADR 0025 — A runner repair passes a targeted check; one full make verify precedes phase 6\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, open is proposed and closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Every runner repair therefore paid for a full `make verify`, even for\na narrow edit. Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* A repair cycle no longer waits for a full run unless its selection is\n  unsafe; the effect on cycle and lane times is not yet measured.\n* A targeted check can miss a test the touch map does not link to a touched\n  file. The full `make verify` before phase 6 catches such a miss before the\n  review, and CI remains the full gate of the pull request.\n* A repair can be marked fixed on a targeted result that the full check\n  later turns red; that red stops phase 6 until it is repaired.\n\n## Validation\n\n* #343 carries the runner implementation and its criterion tests; this\n  pull request carries only the ADR text.\n* CI on this pull request is its gate; merge, not this draft, accepts the ADR.\n\n## Implement and draft amendment — the targeted check covers more verbs, 2026-11-12\n\nThe maintainer answered the interview of the change\n`targeted-check-more-verbs` on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12\n(`plans/changes/targeted-check-more-verbs/decisions.md`, Q-1 to Q-6; bead\ncoding-harne",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "citation": "docs/architecture/2026-09-17-omnigent-first-target.md::Trust and enforcement",
          "end_line": 431,
          "excerpt": "## Trust and enforcement\n\n- **Every rule has an enforcer.** Each binding rule names an enforcer or an\n  owner and dated ramp valve. Gates have known-bad cases and prove they\n  examined the intended inputs; an empty findings list can pass when the\n  reviewed subject is valid and non-empty.\n- **One gate list.** The gate manifest is the sole quality-gate list. Runtime\n  policies enforce permissions around actions; they are not a second list of\n  quality checks.\n- **Workers cannot self-authorize.** Ordinary coding workers cannot change\n  active policy, gate configuration, hooks, the tracker wrapper, protected\n  acceptance fixtures or their own acceptance report.\n- **Harness changes are their own class.** A dedicated harness-maintenance\n  change may propose those edits with declared scope and human review; checks\n  from an approved revision must still assess the transition. Branch-provided\n  gate changes cannot grant themselves authority.\n- **Bypass must be seen to fail.** The pilot proves that an attempted bypass\n  is rejected.\n\n- **External tools are components, not authorities.** External tools and\n  skills are version-pinned, scoped components, not sources of workflow\n  authority. Their prompts, repositories and rule files cannot change\n  permissions, the Beads writer, the gate manifest, review dispositions or\n  human decisions.\n- **Control inputs stay protected.** Protect active review rules,\n  adapter/action definitions and skill instructions as control inputs;\n  evaluate proposed changes with an approved revision. Installation and\n  updates require a reviewed, recorded choice, never an automatic import from\n  repository text or a remote registry. The\n  [CrewAI](../research/2026-09-18-crewai-assessment.md) and\n  [Agent Skills](../research/2026-09-18-agent-skills-assessment.md)\n  assessments retain Omnigent as coordinator and propose only bounded\n  adapter/skill trials.\n\n- **Worktrees share Git.** Worktrees isolate files but share Git resources.\n  The adapter must constrain shells and descendant processes as well as editor\n  tools, including writes via symlinks and to shared Git configuration, hooks\n  and other workers' refs. Git operations are mediated so a worker can commit\n  only to its assigned branch.\n- **If isolation cannot be shown, stop.** If that cannot be demonstrated, pause\n  M0 and propose a stronger isolation layout rather than declaring worktrees a\n  security boundary.\n- **Text is not permission.** Repository text, logs and tool results cannot\n  grant permissions or override the assigned contract. A harmless\n  injected-instruction fixture tests this boundary.\n\n- **Every model call is checked.** Endpoint checks cover every model call,\n  including coordinator, routing and review. Foreign calls also require the\n  disclosure decision and leak check.\n- **Probe the boundaries.** Runtime configuration is pinned, telemetry\n  behavior tested, and required sandbox, secret-path, egress and write\n  boundaries probed on safe fixtures. Terminal and subagent policies must be\n  checked independently on the pinned release.\n- **Record what ran.** The evidence record names effective configurations and\n  their hashes. Logs sent to a model or stored with a PR are subject to the\n  same data rules.\n\n",

          "end_line": 149,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n**(c)**, with these contracts:\n\n* **The architecture delta lives in the change's `design.md`.** A section\n  \"Architecture delta\" holds:\n  1. a Mermaid diagram — a flowchart, the form GitHub renders — of the part\n     of the system the change touches, as it is after the change, each box\n     labelled with its C4 level (person, system, container, component);\n  2. below it, three short lists of elements and relationships: **added**,\n     **changed**, **removed**.\n\n  If nothing architectural moves, one sentence says why.\n* **No model as code in the kit now.** No LikeC4 specification, no `model/`\n  scaffold, no `likec4 build` or `likec4 validate` gate, no Node.js\n  dependency. Elements are named as the existing diagrams and ADRs name\n  them, as in LakeSwitch's D-58.\n* **D-15 is amended.** Its LikeC4 part — the tool, the pinned specification\n  and the build gate — is replaced by the architecture delta. Its arc42 and\n  MADR templates are not touched by this ADR; when the kit ships them stays\n  with the template work.\n* **O-3 is amended in one clause.**\n  * **Kept:** an Architectural change requires an ADR in the same pull\n    request. The ADR duty for architectural changes is unchanged.\n  * **Changed:** \"and a model diff\" becomes \"and a filled 'Architecture\n    delta' section in its `design.md`\".\n  * **Not touched:** the DRIFT rule for a module created, deleted or renamed\n    under `src/` or `spec/` in a change of another class.\n* **LikeC4 stays the upgrade path.** The question returns, as an ADR of its\n  own, when any one of these happens:\n  1. a review records, for the third time, a defect in an Architectural\n     change that a model delta would have caught, and the reviewer names it\n     as such in `findings.md` — LakeSwitch's D-58 trigger, so both\n     repositories move together;\n  2. the same element appears in three or more architecture pictures, and a\n     rename or split had to be made by hand in more than one of them;\n  3. the model grows past about thirty elements — more than one page holds —\n     and an agent's work needs dependency queries across it.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"One runner with stage barriers and provider queues\", because\nit keeps the established entry point while making boundaries and handoff\ncheckable.\n\n1. `stage2.py explore` dispatches features and architectural changes to the\n   swarm, bounded/spike to GLM Flash; explicit Stage-1 fallback remains Haiku\n   5.5 with its reason. Early research/spec/argument classes must agree.\n   Swarm research headers require an explicit neighbours list; [] is valid,\n   while a missing/null/non-list key refuses with exit 2 and a repair message.\n2. Finder step 0 uses the three repository seats as independent\n   locators; Opus 5.5 merges code, rules/ADRs, tests/gates and neighbour lists.\n   The merged finder keys are their exact deduplicated category/reference\n   union with all origins/reasons; extra or missing keys fail preparation.\n   Runner resolution against scratch frozen bytes marks unresolved entries\n   without granting topic scope, then inserts all given neighbours as given.\n   Finder suggestions remain marked rather than silently accepted.\n   Eligible neighbour specs have three forms: plans/changes/<name>/spec.md\n   (one segment other than archive),\n   plans/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD-name>/spec.md, and\n   plans/specs/<capability>/spec.md, excluding the change's own spec. Resolved\n   neighbour-category artifacts inside those folders map to the frozen spec\n   if present, retaining every finder key. Own-change entries are self with\n   no relation/gap; other resolved entries are no-spec with named gaps.\n   Given paths outside those forms or the own spec refuse with exit 2;\n   eligible given paths must exist in frozen bytes.\n3. Topics 1–8 cover code/reuse, callers/interfaces, rules/class, architecture,\n   neighbours, history/volatility, tests/gates and risks; each uses the\n   three repository seats on identical briefs, perspectives and report\n   template.\n   After map merge the runner collects topic 6's local frozen-HEAD history:\n   up to ten most recent commits per resolved mapped path, with full hash,\n   UTC author date, subject, body capped at 4,000 characters with truncation\n   marked, and touched mapped paths. Older history is not read. Only topic 6\n   receives it; a full packet hash resolves to that record, but a reachable\n   hash outside the packet or PR/bead id alone is unsupported. No network or\n   tracker is read; collection failure prevents topics and exits 1 incomplete.\n4. Topics 9–11 cover best practice, existing tools/standards and public failure\n   reports. Each uses the three online seats through Pi with only the\n   filtered Opus sentence, fixed questions and public sources.\n   In addition, every eligible Go chat model ending `-free`, selected from a\n   live-fetched Pi Go overlay with declared include/exclude lists, works each\n   online topic on the same brief. No Zen provider, OpenCode CLI, fixed free\n   roster or substitution for the online seats. Dynamic free\n   permission applies to public-only research, never private roles. Select only\n   fresh-Pi text-input chat entries with exact matching models.dev\n   opencode-go.models keys, with a present id field equal to the key,\n   boolean tool_call true and status not deprecated.\n   Missing/negative support, missing metadata, deprecated, non-chat and\n   baseline-only entries are excluded with reasons. Unavailable/unreadable\n   models.dev excludes all free candidates as capability-unavailable N=0,\n   retaining required slots; this is distinct from a measured empty eligible set.\n   Both sources are dated/digested. Pi refresh failure exits 1 before all\n   models; Pi's absent capability field is expected, never a fallback trigger. These free\n   seats are best-effort: failure is named, never hidden or substituted, and\n   does not alone invalidate the 39 required contributions.\n   Missing/non-object provider/models, non-object root, invalid JSON,\n   non-200/request failure or duplicate claimed ids are document-level\n   capability-unavailable.           "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 89,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## 5 Die Regeln\n\n### A — Agents\n\n| ID | Regel | Stufe | Erzwingender Test/Gate | Gilt in |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **RB-A1** | Ein Agent berichtet nur, was er in dieser Sitzung beobachtet hat; Nicht-Beobachtetes ist `UNKNOWN`, nie `NO`; jede Behauptung trägt `evidence:`; Proxys heißen Proxys; negative Antworten sind nicht symmetrisch; vor einem „liest nichts\"-Urteil folgt er den Imports; er nimmt seine eigene Arbeit nie ab (§6) | 2 | `Ramp:agents-evidence-contract` | P L I |\n| **RB-A2** | Read-only-Agents führen kein `Bash`, `Write` oder `Edit`; wer eine Shell hat, deklariert ihren Umfang; `permissions.deny` enthält mindestens Prod-Deploy, `bundle destroy`, Force-Push und `rm -rf` | 2 | `Ramp:agents-tool-scopes` | P L I |\n| **RB-A3** | Eine selbst erklärte Verifikation ist keine: ein Verdikt gilt erst, wenn ein zweiter unabhängiger Leser oder ein Script es aus den Findings nachgerechnet hat | 2 | `Ramp:skill-outputs-transfer` | P L I |\n| **RB-A4** | Ein schreibender Agent deklariert, wohin er schreiben darf — nie in den Entscheidungs-Baum, nie in seinen eigenen Abnahmebericht —, führt einen Abschnitt „was ein Mensch prüft\" und liefert ein Ergebnis, in dem `UNKNOWN` vorkommen darf | 2 | `Ramp:agent-writes-allowlist` | P L I |\n| **RB-A5** | Wo ein Agent entscheidet, steht ein geschlossenes Vokabular, kein Freitext. The lines stay outside the\n# gate-frame format the evidence parser reads: summary entries have three\n# spaces after `──`, while gate frames require exactly one (`^── \\[`). Thus\n# no skipped gate becomes a gate section, and skipped gates get no timing events: the\n# history describes executed commands only.\nif [ -n \"$verbleibend\" ]; then\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"── not run — the run stopped at the blocking failure in [$stop_gate]:\"\n    printf '%s' \"$verbleibend\" | while IFS= read -r gid; do\n        [ -n \"$gid\" ] && echo \"──   [$gid] not run\"\n    done\nfi\n\n# Execution seconds from the admitted runner's measurement start to its final\n# verdict; the admission wait is reported beside it, never inside it.\nif [ -n \"$RUN_ID\" ]; then\n    duration_verdict=red\n    [ \"$fehler\" -ne 0 ] || duration_verdict=green\n    dur_call exec_t1 clock\n    dur_call duration_summary end --run \"$RUN_ID\" --start \"$exec_t0\" --end \"$exec_t1\" --verdict \"$duration_verdict\"\n    [ -n \"$duration_summary\" ] && echo \"$duration_summary\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\nif [ \"$fehler\" -ne 0 ]; then\n    echo \"VERIFY RED — at least one gate failed; the report above names it.\"\n    exit 1\nfi\necho \"VERIFY GREEN — every local gate of the '$JOB' job passed.\"\nexit 0\n",

          "excerpt": "def catalog_rows(alle: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The one list as a Markdown table — the inventory of docs/governance/gate-catalog.md.\n\n    Deterministic and unfiltered: every declared gate, in list order, with the\n    fields the catalog promises (id, title, command or action, job,\n    enforcement, cost, floor, placement, reason — the cost column since\n    schema 3, bead coding-harness-bxxt.1). A command gate and a hosted action\n    are rendered distinctly, and an action with a local equivalent names it —\n    the reader must see what runs where. `tests/test_gate_catalog.py` holds\n    the committed inventory to this rendering.\n    \"\"\"\n    if alle is None:\n        alle = gates()\n    zeilen = [\n        \"| id | title | command / action | job | enforcement | cost | floor | placement | reason |\",\n        \"|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\",\n    ]\n    for g in alle:\n        if g[\"action\"]:\n            einsatz = f\"action `{g['action']}` (hosted CI only)\"\n            if g[\"via_local_equivalent\"]:\n                einsatz = f\"action `{g['action']}`; locally: `{g['command']}`\"\n        else:\n            einsatz = f\"`{g['command']}`\"\n        kosten_zelle = f\"{_zelle(g['cost'])} | \"\n        zeilen.append(\n            f\"| {_zelle(g['id'])} | {_zelle(g['name'])} | {_zelle(einsatz)} | {_zelle(g['job'])} | \"\n            f\"{_zelle(g['enforcement'])} | {kosten_zelle}{'yes' if g['floor'] else 'no'} | {_zelle(g['placement'])} | \"\n            f\"{_zelle(g['reason'])} |\"\n        )\n    return \"\\n\".join(zeilen)\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_catalog_drift_is_rejected() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2: a mutated inventory or a changed declaration leaves the comparison red.\n\n    Each case plants the fault the spec refutes with, on fixture data; the\n    first assertion is the counter-check that the comparator itself is green\n    on a clean render.\n    \"\"\"\n    alle = _fixture_gates()\n    rows = _rows(catalog_rows(alle))\n    assert _drift(alle, rows) == [], \"the clean render must pass its own comparison\"\n\n    assert _drift(alle, rows[:2]) == [\"missing row: probe-equivalent\"]\n\n    fremd = {**rows[0], \"id\": \"probe-foreign\"}\n    assert _drift(alle, [*rows, fremd]) == [\"extra row: probe-foreign\"]\n    assert _drift(alle, [*rows, rows[0]]) == [\"duplicate row: probe-command\"]\n\n    gelogen = {**rows[1], \"enforcement\": \"block\"}\n    assert _drift(alle, [rows[0], gelogen, rows[2]]) == [\n        \"probe-hosted: enforcement reads 'block', the gate declares 'advisory'\"\n    ]\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n**(c)**, with these contracts:\n\n* **The architecture delta lives in the change's `design.md`.** A section\n  \"Architecture delta\" holds:\n  1. a Mermaid diagram — a flowchart, the form GitHub renders — of the part\n     of the system the change touches, as it is after the change, each box\n     labelled with its C4 level (person, system, container, component);\n  2. below it, three short lists of elements and relationships: **added**,\n     **changed**, **removed**.\n\n  If nothing architectural moves, one sentence says why.\n* **No model as code in the kit now.** No LikeC4 specification, no `model/`\n  scaffold, no `likec4 build` or `likec4 validate` gate, no Node.js\n  dependency. Elements are named as the existing diagrams and ADRs name\n  them, as in LakeSwitch's D-58.\n* **D-15 is amended.** Its LikeC4 part — the tool, the pinned specification\n  and the build gate — is replaced by the architecture delta. Its arc42 and\n  MADR templates are not touched by this ADR; when the kit ships them stays\n  with the template work.\n* **O-3 is amended in one clause.**\n  * **Kept:** an Architectural change requires an ADR in the same pull\n    request. The ADR duty for architectural changes is unchanged.\n  * **Changed:** \"and a model diff\" becomes \"and a filled 'Architecture\n    delta' section in its `design.md`\".\n  * **Not touched:** the DRIFT rule for a module created, deleted or renamed\n    under `src/` or `spec/` in a change of another class.\n* **LikeC4 stays the upgrade path.** The question returns, as an ADR of its\n  own, when any one of these happens:\n  1. a review records, for the third time, a defect in an Architectural\n     change that a model delta would have caught, and the reviewer names it\n     as such in `findings.md` — LakeSwitch's D-58 trigger, so both\n     repositories move together;\n  2. the same element appears in three or more architecture pictures, and a\n     rename or split had to be made by hand in more than one of them;\n  3. the model grows past about thirty elements — more than one page holds —\n     and an agent's work needs dependency queries across it.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-6 · How the runner keeps pytest inside the run area\n\nasked: 2026-11-13\nanswer: \"Ja\" to the plugin solution — a small pytest plugin the runner loads into every pytest run checks, in pytest_configure, the temporary folder pytest itself resolved and stops the run with a clear message when it lies outside this run's area; the runner's own parser for PYTEST_ADDOPTS goes.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the change verify-tmp-cleanup (bead coding-harness-bxxt.3), phase-6 finding F6-1.\n  Intention: Codex showed two more spellings (-o=addopts=…, @args.txt) by which a caller can give pytest its own basetemp; the second finding of this mechanism after L2-12.\n  Today: the runner parses PYTEST_ADDOPTS to refuse --basetemp; each rule misses the next spelling. Pydantic or Jinja do not help: only pytest knows what it makes of its option sources.\n  Repository change: a plugin of about fifteen lines, the parser in scripts/verify_all.sh removed, tests for the spellings.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of pytest options that arrive through several channels,\nfacing a parser of our own that misses each new spelling,\nwe decided that a plugin asks pytest for the temporary folder it resolved and stops a run outside the area,\nto achieve one check that covers every spelling,\naccepting a plugin loaded into every pytest run of make verify — 2026-11-13\n\n",
