          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **ADR edit** — a path under `docs/adr/` in the measured diff. Which states\n  the diff holds and which base it is taken against stay as the gate has them\n  today: committed, staged, unstaged and untracked paths, a rename seen as a\n  removal and an addition.\n- **Claim** — the list `adr_files` in the header of a change's `spec.md`: the\n  paths under `docs/adr/` the change creates, changes or removes. A\n  **claimable path** begins `docs/adr/`, names a file below that folder, and\n  holds no empty, `.` or `..` segment. A header without the field claims\n  nothing, and so does `adr_files: []` (amended 2026-10-13 after phase-6 row\n  F-6: the field is recognised by the parsed key in any YAML spelling, and a\n  header that does not parse as YAML is reported, since it cannot be decided\n  whether it claims).\n- **Changes of the diff** — the active change folders, directly under\n  `plans/changes/` and not `archive/`, that hold at least one path of the\n  measured diff, whichever file it is.\n- **Claimant** — of an ADR edit: a change of the diff whose claim lists the\n  edit's path.\n- **Adoption record** — `decisions/adoption.yaml`: per repository, the day it\n  adopted each gate that exempts the changes begun before it, keyed by the\n  gate's id in `decisions/gates.yaml`. It stays in its repository and does not\n  travel with the kit (`design.md`).\n- **Adoption day** — the day the adoption record holds for\n  `interview-minimums`.\n- **Subject** — a change whose spec `date` is later than the adoption day,\n  active or archived: the rule the cut-off holds today, with the adoption day\n  in place of the constant. A change whose date cannot be read stays subject.\n- **The gate** — `scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`, gate id\n  `interview-minimums`. **The reader** — `scripts/adoption.py`, the one module\n  that reads the adoption record.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Where a missing decision statement is prevented\n\nasked: 2026-11-10\nanswer: \"Kann bei sowas pydantic oder jinja 2 helfen? A\" — option A of the dialog, which was \"both\": the interview asks the accepted downside with every question and writes the statement at once, and `draft` refuses before its first model call when a statement is missing. The question about pydantic and Jinja2 in the same answer is recorded as a [GAP] for the spec.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where it is made sure that every interview answer carries its decision statement in decisions.md.\n  Intention: in the night of 2026-11-10 two changes (verify-slots, review-fewer-rounds) lost three draft attempts each on the missing statement alone.\n  Today: the interview prompt holds a template line for the statement; the accepted downside is not asked; a draft notices the gap only after its model calls, in the document check.\n  Repository change: the interview prompt, the runner's draft verb and tests; no new gate.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the decision statement that every answered interview record\nneeds, facing drafts that failed after their model calls on the missing\nstatement alone, we decided that the interview asks the accepted downside\nwith every question and writes the statement at once, and that `draft`\nrefuses before its first model call when a statement is missing, to achieve\nthat no draft attempt is spent on a missing statement, accepting that every\ninterview question gets a little longer, because the maintainer chooses the\ndownside with the answer — 2026-11-10\n\n",

          "end_line": 129,

          "excerpt": "## Q-6 · How the runner keeps pytest inside the run area\n\nasked: 2026-11-13\nanswer: \"Ja\" to the plugin solution — a small pytest plugin the runner loads into every pytest run checks, in pytest_configure, the temporary folder pytest itself resolved and stops the run with a clear message when it lies outside this run's area; the runner's own parser for PYTEST_ADDOPTS goes.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the change verify-tmp-cleanup (bead coding-harness-bxxt.3), phase-6 finding F6-1.\n  Intention: Codex showed two more spellings (-o=addopts=…, @args.txt) by which a caller can give pytest its own basetemp; the second finding of this mechanism after L2-12.\n  Today: the runner parses PYTEST_ADDOPTS to refuse --basetemp; each rule misses the next spelling. Pydantic or Jinja do not help: only pytest knows what it makes of its option sources.\n  Repository change: a plugin of about fifteen lines, the parser in scripts/verify_all.sh removed, tests for the spellings.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of pytest options that arrive through several channels,\nfacing a parser of our own that misses each new spelling,\nwe decided that a plugin asks pytest for the temporary folder it resolved and stops a run outside the area,\nto achieve one check that covers every spelling,\naccepting a plugin loaded into every pytest run of make verify — 2026-11-13\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Publication** — an accepted single-model answer or a runner-written swarm\n  record, including an incomplete swarm publication; a call audit alone, a\n  failed answer, quoted text or a fenced example is not publication.\n- **Active research** — `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` directly under each\n  active change folder, excluding `archive/`. Existing model attribution or\n  accepted publication evidence establishes model-written research regardless\n  of its current provenance label, including manually seeded work.\n- **Stock exemption** — the adoption day recorded for the census in\n  `decisions/adoption.yaml` (maintainer, `decisions.md` Q-5 and option C,\n  2026-11-12), applied at one place in `scripts/research_census.py`. An active\n  research file is stock only when it is unchanged in the working tree and its\n  last change in Git was committed before that day: its findings are not\n  reported. Dates and producer evidence inside the file do not decide the\n  exemption. Uncommitted files or unreadable Git history are subject to the\n  census. The removed fixed\n  `UNCORRECTED` file set is no longer required anywhere. Stock files await the\n  separate history-based correction (bead coding-harness-2i7x — normalise\n  existing research).\n- **Skeleton text** — only the generated opening empty-file paragraph and\n  provenance-instruction blockquote from `scripts/new_change.py`; the title and\n  authored quotations of those notices remain research.\n- **Producer attribution** — one producer record, or a non-empty list for\n  several known contributions. Records identify the producing program or swarm\n  orchestration and its evidence-backed date; known model identities and earlier\n  contributions remain represented. A swarm record does not attribute the\n  whole document to one participant.\n- **Metadata contract** — exactly one top-level `provenance`, `produced_by`,\n  `review`, `date`, `last_reviewed` and `updated` field, without duplicate keys\n  inside producer/review mappings; `ai-drafted-reviewed` provenance; non-empty\n  producer attribution; pending review with null approver and approval date.\n  Every producer has `kind: llm-session`, an evidence-backed program name and\n  an ISO calendar date string in `version`; known models are retained separately.\n  Dates obey `date <= last_reviewed <= updated`, and producer dates lie within\n  `date..updated`. The edit stamp is the actual edit day, without inventing a\n  historical publication or human review date.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Address record:** the existing `adresse` mapping on the `opencode-go`\n  entry of `model-endpoints.yaml`, with its host and bases keyed by wire API.\n- **Wire API:** the model definition's `api`, identifying its request format;\n  an API differs here when its name is absent from the record's API keys.\n  Any API present in that record is compared with its own recorded base.\n- **Address-admissible row:** a definition accepted by the existing address\n  policy; this alone grants neither model eligibility nor permission to send.\n\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/ontology-relation-layer/research.md::The architecture this research proposes",
          "end_line": 237,
          "excerpt": "## The architecture this research proposes\n\nThree pieces, one direction. Each piece is a child bead; none is a new artefact\ntype.\n\n```\n  files in the tree            one declaration            findings\n  (markdown + yaml)     ->     (pydantic models)    ->    (gates, red)\n        |                            ^\n        |                            |\n        +---- jinja2 renders --------+     no write-back, ever\n```\n\n1. **Schema.** The relations are declared once, as models: `Gate`, `Rule`,\n   `Decision`, `Change`, `ProvenanceClass`, `Bead`. Closed enums and field\n   constraints are taken verbatim from `decisions/gates.yaml` and\n   `provenance.yaml` — those files stay the declaration of record; the models\n   are their typed form. A relation that is not a field cannot be written into\n   an artefact.\n2. **Rendering.** The headers that are typed by hand today come from the model:\n   `scripts/new_change.py` and the kit templates render through one Jinja2\n   template. A hand edit stays possible — but the gate then validates against\n   the model, not against a second regex.\n3. **Edges, one reasoner.** One projection turns frontmatter plus\n   `gates.yaml` plus the bead export into typed edges **in memory**. Nothing is\n   stored; the projection is rebuilt on every run, in the way `ki` rebuilds its\n   Neo4j index from a folder of Markdown and never writes to the source.\n\n**Acceptance, measurable.** A gate that is red when a rule loses its last gate.\nA gate that is red when two artefacts claim the same functional relation. One\nhand-written header parser fewer than today, counted by the gate that bead\ncoding-harness-rg8i introduces. The findings of the four checks above unchanged\nor lower at the head of the change.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

A file\n   under `optional`, `none` or no entry is never held, whether or not it\n   carries frontmatter.\n   *Refuted by:* a temporary repository in which a stale file under an\n   `optional`, `none`, unmapped or excluded prefix is reported, a stale file\n   under `required` is not, or a shorter prefix wins over a longer one.\n\n2. **What is reported.** A held file is reported when it has no frontmatter\n   block; when the block has no top-level `updated:` line, more than one, or a\n   value that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date (quoted or not); when `updated:` is\n   earlier than the file's reference date; or when `updated:` is later than the\n   UTC date at run time plus one day. Nothing else is reported.\n   *Refuted by:* any of these cases exiting 0 in a temporary repository, or a\n   held file whose `updated:` equals its reference date being reported.\n\n3. **The reference date.** For a held file whose content equals `HEAD`, it is\n   the committer date — as a calendar date in the offset recorded in that\n   commit — of the newest non-merge commit that changed the file at its\n   current path, under git's default history simplification\n   (`git log -1 --no-merges --format=%cs -- <path>`). A rename or move to the\n   current path counts as a change. A merge commit never counts, including the\n   merge commit GitHub builds for a pull request. Exit 1\n   when something is: one line per file with the path, the finding and — for a\n   stale file — both dates, then the fix\n   `python3 scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py --stamp` verbatim.           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. **Held files come from the map.** A file is held exactly when it is a\n   Markdown file (`*.md`), tracked or untracked-but-not-ignored, present on\n   disk, not under an `excluded:` prefix of `provenance.yaml`, and the longest\n   `paths:` prefix that matches it declares `frontmatter: required`. A file\n   under `optional`, `none` or no entry is never held, whether or not it\n   carries frontmatter.\n   *Refuted by:* a temporary repository in which a stale file under an\n   `optional`, `none`, unmapped or excluded prefix is reported, a stale file\n   under `required` is not, or a shorter prefix wins over a longer one.\n\n2. **What is reported.** A held file is reported when it has no frontmatter\n   block; when the block has no top-level `updated:` line, more than one, or a\n   value that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date (quoted or not); when `updated:` is\n   earlier than the file's reference date; or when `updated:` is later than the\n   UTC date at run time plus one day. Nothing else is reported.\n   *Refuted by:* any of these cases exiting 0 in a temporary repository, or a\n   held file whose `updated:` equals its reference date being reported.\n\n3. **The reference date.** For a held file whose content equals `HEAD`, it is\n   the committer date — as a calendar date in the offset recorded in that\n   commit — of the newest non-merge commit that changed the file at its\n   current path, under git's default history simplification\n   (`git log -1 --no-merges --format=%cs -- <path>`). A rename or move to the\n   current path counts as a change. A merge commit never counts, including the\n   merge commit GitHub builds for a pull request. For a held file that is\n   untracked or differs from `HEAD` in the index or the worktree, the reference\n   date is today on the running machine's clock and timezone.\n   *Refuted by,* each in a temporary repository: a body change committed a day\n   after the stamp that exits 0; a `git mv` committed a day after the stamp\n   that exits 0; a file changed only on a branch, stamped on the day of the\n   branch commit and merged with `--no-ff` days later, that is reported; a\n   commit made at 23:30 −05:00 whose stamp names that local day being\n   reported; an uncommitted edit under yesterday's stamp that exits 0.\n\n4. **Exit codes and the message.** Exit 0 when nothing is reported. Exit 1\n   when something is: one line per file with the path, the finding and — for a\n   stale file — both dates, then the fix\n   `python3 scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py --stamp` verbatim. Exit 3,\n   measuring nothing, when the repository is shallow (the message names\n   `fetch-depth: 0`), when the path is not a git work tree or has no commit,\n   or when `provenance.yaml` cannot be read.\n   *Refuted by:* a `--depth 1` clone that exits 0 or 1; a failing run whose\n   output lacks the fix command.\n\n5. **The stamp.** `--stamp` sets `updated:` to today's local date in every held\n   file reported for a missing, unreadable, stale or future `updated:`. It\n   replaces that one line or, when the line is missing, inserts it directly\n   after the top-level `last_reviewed:` line, or else as the last line of the\n   block. It changes no other byte.           "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Publication** — an accepted single-model answer or a runner-written swarm\n  record, including an incomplete swarm publication; a call audit alone, a\n  failed answer, quoted text or a fenced example is not publication.\n- **Active research** — `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` directly under each\n  active change folder, excluding `archive/`. Existing model attribution or\n  accepted publication evidence establishes model-written research regardless\n  of its current provenance label, including manually seeded work.\n- **Stock exemption** — the adoption day recorded for the census in\n  `decisions/adoption.yaml` (maintainer, `decisions.md` Q-5 and option C,\n  2026-11-12), applied at one place in `scripts/research_census.py`. An active\n  research file is stock only when it is unchanged in the working tree and its\n  last change in Git was committed before that day: its findings are not\n  reported. Dates and producer evidence inside the file do not decide the\n  exemption. Uncommitted files or unreadable Git history are subject to the\n  census. The removed fixed\n  `UNCORRECTED` file set is no longer required anywhere. Stock files await the\n  separate history-based correction (bead coding-harness-2i7x — normalise\n  existing research).\n- **Skeleton text** — only the generated opening empty-file paragraph and\n  provenance-instruction blockquote from `scripts/new_change.py`; the title and\n  authored quotations of those notices remain research.\n- **Producer attribution** — one producer record, or a non-empty list for\n  several known contributions. Records identify the producing program or swarm\n  orchestration and its evidence-backed date; known model identities and earlier\n  contributions remain represented. A swarm record does not attribute the\n  whole document to one participant.\n- **Metadata contract** — exactly one top-level `provenance`, `produced_by`,\n  `review`, `date`, `last_reviewed` and `updated` field, without duplicate keys\n  inside producer/review mappings; `ai-drafted-reviewed` provenance; non-empty\n  producer attribution; pending review with null approver and approval date.\n  Every producer has `kind: llm-session`, an evidence-backed program name and\n  an ISO calendar date string in `version`; known models are retained separately.\n  Dates obey `date <= last_reviewed <= updated`, and producer dates lie within\n  `date..updated`. The edit stamp is the actual edit day, without inventing a\n  historical publication or human review date.\n\n",

          "end_line": 142,
          "excerpt": "## Q-6 · How the runner keeps pytest inside the run area\n\nasked: 2026-11-13\nanswer: \"Ja\" to the plugin solution — a small pytest plugin the runner loads into every pytest run checks, in pytest_configure, the temporary folder pytest itself resolved and stops the run with a clear message when it lies outside this run's area; the runner's own parser for PYTEST_ADDOPTS goes.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the change verify-tmp-cleanup (bead coding-harness-bxxt.3), phase-6 finding F6-1.\n  Intention: Codex showed two more spellings (-o=addopts=…, @args.txt) by which a caller can give pytest its own basetemp; the second finding of this mechanism after L2-12.\n  Today: the runner parses PYTEST_ADDOPTS to refuse --basetemp; each rule misses the next spelling. Pydantic or Jinja do not help: only pytest knows what it makes of its option sources.\n  Repository change: a plugin of about fifteen lines, the parser in scripts/verify_all.sh removed, tests for the spellings.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of pytest options that arrive through several channels,\nfacing a parser of our own that misses each new spelling,\nwe decided that a plugin asks pytest for the temporary folder it resolved and stops a run outside the area,\nto achieve one check that covers every spelling,\naccepting a plugin loaded into every pytest run of make verify — 2026-11-13\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "## Problem\n\nA document's header can say the document is older than its content, and\nnothing notices. The maintainer asked for a basic mechanism that keeps headers\ncurrent and stops a stale one from being merged (`decisions.md`, items 1–2).\nToday (`research.md`, corrections and addendum, measured on `9f14283`):\n\n- No header records when its content last changed. `updated:` stands in 0 of\n  30 `docs/` files with frontmatter; `last_reviewed` records a review, not a\n  change.\n- `provenance.yaml` declares per prefix whether a file must carry frontmatter,\n  but nothing reads that field. The documents the maintainer named are not all\n  declared: `docs/adr/`, `docs/how-to/` and `docs/governance/` are `optional`,\n  `docs/architecture/` and `docs/research/` have no entry, and\n  `.claude/agents/` — excluded by the maintainer — is `required`.\n- The six ADRs carry no frontmatter at all.\n- The hosted checkout has one commit of history. In CI, `git log -1 -- <file>`\n  returns the checked-out commit for every file — on a pull request, GitHub's\n  merge commit, dated the day of the run. The generated checkout step has no\n  `with:`, so no gate can ask for more history.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }

          "end_line": 59,
          "excerpt": "## Problem\n\n- **The gate infers an ADR's owner from the diff.** Every active change folder\n  with a file in the measured diff is an owner, and exactly one is required\n  (`research.md`, Q1, read at `2d6a1c6`). A change that adds an ADR and touches\n  another change folder for any reason goes red: criterion-test-ledger adds\n  ADR 0013 beside four migrated plans (bead `coding-harness-afa`).\n- **The repair of pull request #126 guesses.** It treats a folder touched\n  through `plan.md` alone as no owner and, beside another owner, lets the ADR\n  text decide; its own docstring calls the rule interim, and any other\n  cross-folder edit breaks it again (`research.md`, \"Corrections after\n  verification\", read at `7f53552`).\n- **Nothing states an ADR's owner.** An answer file binds a change to its\n  answer, never an ADR to a change; `owner:` in an ADR header names a role, and\n  no ADR carries a change name (`research.md`, Q2).\n- **A \"yes\" is not held to an ADR.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §2 says it itself:\n  \"Nothing checks … that a 'yes' is followed by an ADR\" (`research.md`, Q3).\n- **The gate stays home, and its cut-off is this repository's.** The kit\n  manifest has no entry for `scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`, while the\n  gate list that runs it travels; the cut-off is a constant in the script,\n  2026-10-08, the day this repository adopted the gate; the criterion-ledger\n  gate of #126 has the same shape (bead `coding-harness-wpv`; `research.md`,\n  Q4 and \"Corrections after verification\").\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-adr-owning-change/spec.md",
          "reference": "Problem",

          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false

          "excerpt": "# ontology relation layer — Research\n\nPhase 1 per [`prompts/01-explore.md`](../../../prompts/01-explore.md). The question\ncomes from the maintainer on 2026-11-18: *what does an ontology buy this\nrepository, and can it secure that rules are followed?* The answer this\nexploration arrives at is narrower than the word suggests, and it is the reason\nthe change exists: **not a knowledge base beside the repository, but one typed\nrelation layer that the gates read instead of eleven private parsers.**\n\nMeasured at `origin/main` `fd2b8701`, 2026-11-18. Every count below carries that\ncommit.\n\n## What an ontology is, in plain words\n\nAn ontology is a machine-readable map of a field: **which things exist, which\nrelations between them are allowed, and what is forbidden.** It is a schema with\nmeaning, not just a data structure. A table says \"this column is text\"; an\nontology says \"this is a gate, and a gate belongs to exactly one rule\".\n\nThree properties matter for this repository:\n\n- **Named relations.** \"A rule is protected by a gate\" is an edge with a name,\n  so a program can ask about it. Prose cannot be asked.\n- **Constraints.** A *functional* relation holds once (one father, one status).\n  A *disjoint* pair never coincides (customer and support agent). A violation is\n  a finding, not a discussion. Frank Coyle's examples are exactly this shape: a\n  second refund on the same order, a payout to the wrong role, a status nobody\n  defined.\n- **Inference.** From two stated facts a reasoner derives a third. raise ValueError(\"empty producer list\")\n    result = []\n    for record in records:\n        if not isinstance(record, dict) or record.get(\"kind\") != \"llm-session\":\n            raise           "excerpt": "## 7 Änderungsverlauf\n\nAppend-only. Jeder Eintrag trägt die vier Pflichtzeilen aus §4.\n\n### 6.0.0 — 2026-10-30\n\n**RB-G7** accepts a merge queue as the freshness requirement. Updating every\nbehind branch before its merge changed the heads against which merges were\narmed and cost one CI run per merge (eight sequential merges on 2026-10-30).\nA merge queue tests each group on GitHub's merge candidate against the\ncurrent `main` and merges exactly that. Decided by the maintainer on\n2026-10-28 (change `merge-queue`, bead `coding-harness-eh42`). The rule text\ntakes effect with the merge of its decision pull request; the queue itself is\nswitched on afterwards, by a separate step on GitHub, and until then the\nup-to-date alternative carries RB-G7.\n\nMAJOR, because §4 says so: the rule's meaning changes — freshness may now come\nfrom either of two alternatives, and CI must also run on merge groups.\n\n- **Geändert:** RB-G7 — its second and third sentences: CI checks the pull request's merge ref and, in a queue, the merge group's ref; freshness comes from a merge queue or from the up-to-date requirement. enforcers extended by `tests/test_ci.py::test_merge_groups_run_the_gates_on_their_candidate`, `tests/test_ci.py::test_merge_groups_require_a_successful_summary`, `tests/test_repo_settings.py::test_merge_queue_supplies_freshness`, `::test_queue_supplier_is_measured_without_bypass` and `::test_queue_preserves_the_other_ruleset_requirements`; level (4) and scope unchanged. No id changed, none removed\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_repo_settings.py` accepts either alternative, holds a queue-only ruleset to the same fail-closed bypass measurement, and keeps every other floor requirement; `tests/test_ci.py` requires the `merge_group` trigger and the gate and summary jobs to run on it\n- **Agents/Hooks/Templates:** `prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\", admits to the queue when it is active and keeps the branch update only for the strict alternative; `templates/repo-settings.md` describes both alternatives; `docs/governance/quality-gates.md` explains MG-2 for both; `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"Pull requests stay mergeable\", has the queue admission procedure, and its one-line summary in `AGENTS.md` names the queue\n- **lakeswitch-ai:** nothing required — its ruleset still meets RB-G7 by the up-to-date alternative; adopting the queue there is a follow-up for that repository, not done here\n\n### 5.0.0 — 2026-10-08\n\n**RB-G7** prüft den Merge-Stand jetzt ganz. Die CI prüft den Merge-Ref des\nPull Requests (`refs/pull/N/merge`). Das allein reichte nicht: er wird\nberechnet, wenn die CI läuft, und bewegt sich `main` vorher, bleibt `verify`\ngrün für einen Merge gegen ein älteres `main`. Darum verlangt das Ruleset\njetzt, dass ein Branch vor dem Merge auf dem Stand seines Ziels ist.\nEntschieden vom Maintainer am 2026-10-08 (Änderung `rb-g7-merge-freshness`,\nBead `coding-harness-34z`).\n\nMAJOR, weil §4 es so vorschreibt: die beiden Sätze der Regel bleiben, aber\nsie verlangt mehr als vorher — jedes Repository, in dem sie gilt, braucht\ndie Ruleset-Einstellung „Require branches to be up to date before merging\".\n\n- **Geändert:** RB-G7 — zwei Sätze angefügt (was CI und Ruleset prüfen, und dass nur die Maschine des Maintainers misst, ob das Ruleset es verlangt — §3, Stufe 4); Erzwinger um `tests/test_ci.py::test_the_verification_runs_against_the_merge_ref` und `tests/test_repo_settings.py::test_master_has_a_ruleset_with_required_checks` ergänzt, `Ramp:merge-freshness` entfällt; Stufe (4) und Geltung unverändert. Keine ID geändert, keine entfernt\n- **Tests:** neu `tests/test_ci.py::test_the_verification_runs_against_the_merge_ref` samt eingepflanzten Fehlern; `tests/test_repo_settings.py` verlangt als sechste Anforderung den aktuellen Branch (`strict_required_status_checks_policy`), gemessen im Gate `ruleset` auf der Maschine des Maintainers, ni",

          "end_line": 168,
          "excerpt": "## Two libraries are declared and unused\n\n`pyproject.toml:20-22` declares `Jinja2==3.1.6`, `pydantic==2.13.5`,\n`pydantic-core==2.46.5`. **No script under `scripts/` imports either library**\n(grep for `import pydantic`, `from pydantic`, `import jinja2`, `from jinja2`,\n2026-11-18). The only mention is `tests/test_lock.py`, which holds the lock file\nto the declarations.\n\nThe same absence shows in `templates/`: ten files (`adr.md`, `spec.md`,\n`design.md`, `findings.md`, `handover.md`, `gate-record.yaml`, `arc42.md`, and\nthree agent documents), and not one carries a Jinja2 marker.\n\nSo the repository already installed the two mechanisms that would make rules\nenforceable, and then wrote its own:\n\n- **Pydantic would make a rule a type.** What stands in its place is the\n  `REQUIRED = (\"status\", \"implementation_status\", \"date\", \"last_reviewed\",\n  \"bead\")` tuple in `scripts/plans_registry.py:39` plus forty lines of\n  hand-written checks after it.\n- **Jinja2 would make an artefact a rendering.** What stands in its place is\n  `_frontmatter_template()` in `scripts/new_change.py:80`, an f-string that\n  hard-codes the header every change folder receives.\n\nThat is the finding this research rests on. The maintainer's question — *how do\nwe secure that rules are followed?* — has an answer that is smaller than an\nontology and more useful: **one declaration of the relations, one renderer, one\nvalidator, one direction.**\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## What is unclear\n\n- Whether the rule registry (bead coding-harness-73gi) should own the `Rule`\n  model, or this change should, and 73gi then consumes it. [DECISION]\n- Which relations belong to the closed vocabulary. Eight are proposed\n  (`protects`, `answers`, `claims`, `derives-from`, `supersedes`,\n  `belongs-to`, `blocks`, `cites`); the spec has to fix the set, because a\n  vocabulary that grows is not a vocabulary.\n- Whether Jinja2 renders the artefacts or only validates the rendered text\n  against the model. Rendering is the stronger guarantee; it also moves the\n  template out of the author's hand.\n- Whether the reasoner becomes a new gate or absorbs the four existing ones.\n  Absorbing them means their findings text moves; that is a reviewable change\n  in itself.\n- How the kit carries all of this into an instance without shipping a\n  repository's own vocabulary as if it were law.\n- Whether `RESEARCH_PROGRAMS` in `scripts/stage2.py:1385` should admit a session\n  that is not one of its four programs. The\n        # search below would instead accept every file that merely MENTIONS\n        # the path — on 2026-09-08 that made `test_workflow_entry.py` the\n        # evidence for `ruleset-drift`, because it names the name in a list\n        # and has some mutation evidence of its own. A coverage that assumes\n        # from a mention covers nothing.\n        return [\n            f\"{p.name}::{m}\"\n            for p, text in sources.items()\n            if p.as_posix().endswith(script)\n            for m in MUTATIONS_NAMEN.findall(text)\n        ]\n    # A script is evidenced by a mutation-named test that REACHES it, not by a\n    # file that names it (bead coding-harness-a05, maintainer 2026-10-21, option\n    # B). On 2026-10-20 a call-site test named the plans-registry renderer only to\n    # identify a command, and the ratchet called both plans-registry exceptions\n    # stale although no test seeds a fault into the renderer.\n    return [f\"{p.name}::{t}\" for p, text in sources.items() for t in _tests_reaching(text, script)]\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "reference": "evidence",

          "end_line": 43,
          "excerpt": "def pruefling(gate: dict) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The subject of this gate — the script it runs.\"\"\"\n    befehl = gate.get(\"command\") or \"\"\n    # The subfolder has to be included: until 2026-09-08 the pattern ended before\n    # the second `/`, and a script under `scripts/kit/` was invisible to the\n    # ratchet — it reported \"no script recognisable\" and demanded an exception\n    # for a gate that had long had its mutation evidence.\n    m = re.search(r\"(?:scripts|docs/patterns)/(?:[A-Za-z_]+/)*([A-Za-z_]+\\.py)\", befehl)\n    if m:\n        return m.group(1)\n    # A gate can also run a test file itself — `ruleset-drift` checks a statement\n    # about the repo configuration for which there is no script and there should\n    # be none: a tool that can change rulesets would be a greater risk than the\n    # finding it makes. Its mutation evidence then lies in exactly that file, and\n    # that is where the ratchet looks for it too.\n    m = re.search(r\"(tests/[A-Za-z_]+\\.py)\", befehl)\n    return m.group(1) if m else \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def _enforcer_da(ref: str) -> bool:\n    if ref.startswith(\"Ramp:\"):\n        return True\n    if ref.startswith(\"lakeswitch:\"):\n        return True\n    if ref.startswith(\"ci.yml#\"):\n        return f\"id: {ref.split('#', 1)[1]}\" in CI_FILE.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    if \"::\" not in ref:\n        return (REPO_ROOT / ref).exists()\n    datei, funktion = ref.split(\"::\", 1)\n    pfad = REPO_ROOT / datei\n    if not pfad.is_file():\n        return False\n    return re.search(rf\"^def {re.escape(funktion)}\\(\", pfad.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"), re.M) is not None\n",

          "excerpt": "def _frontmatter_template(name: str, bead: str, owner: str, heute: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Frontmatter with every field from `plans_registry.REQUIRED` filled in.\n\n    Order and extra fields follow `plans/_README.md` — `supersedes` and\n    `superseded_by` are the only two fields that may be `null`.\n\n    `provenance: human-written` and **no** `produced_by` block: this file was\n    written by a deterministic call that a human issued. It used to say\n    `ai-drafted-reviewed` with\n    `produced_by: {kind: llm-session, name: unknown}` — a provenance that\n    nobody had at the time of writing, and that the provenance gate cannot\n    refute, because `plans/` permits exactly the two classes `human-written`\n    and `ai-drafted-reviewed`. Whoever fills the body with a language model\n    brings both up to date; the generated text says so.\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"\"\"---\ntitle: \"Research — {name}\"\nstatus: draft\nimplementation_status: none\ndate: {heute}\nlast_reviewed: {heute}\nupdated: {heute}\nsupersedes: null\nsuperseded_by: null\nbead: {bead}\nowner: {owner}\nprovenance: human-written\ntags: [research]\n---\n\n\"\"\"\n",

          "truncated": false

          "excerpt": "def header_problems(name: str, root: Path, *, answers: bool, placed_as: str = \"findings.md\") -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"What the gates say about the filled-in example header, placed as a file under `plans/changes/`.\"\"\"\n    text = f\"---\\n{fill(example_header(name))}\\n---\\n\\n# Body\\n\"\n    path = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / CHANGE / (\"spec.md\" if answers else placed_as)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    meta = plans_registry._frontmatter(path)\n    if meta is None:\n        return [\"no readable header\"]\n    problems = []\n    for key in plans_registry.REQUIRED:\n        if key not in meta:\n            problems.append(f\"{key} is missing\")\n        elif meta[key] in (None, \"\"):\n            problems.append(f\"{key} is empty\")\n    if meta.get(\"status\") not in plans_registry.STATUS:\n        problems.append(f\"status {meta.get('status')!r} is refused\")\n    if meta.get(\"implementation_status\") not in plans_registry.IMPLEMENTATION:\n        problems.append(f\"implementation_status {meta.get('implementation_status')!r} is refused\")\n    if not isinstance(frontmatter_current.read_updated(text), date):\n        problems.append(\"no date from read_updated\")\n    if answers:\n        wanted = f\"adr-answers: {CHANGE}: no answer\"\n        lines = adr_answers.examine(root).lines()\n        problems += [line for line in lines if not line.startswith(wanted)]\n        if not any(line.startswith(wanted) for line in lines):\n            problems.append(\"the header is not read as a feature that owes its answer\")\n    return problems\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_templates.py",
          "reference": "header_problems",
          "start_line": 249,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "excerpt": "def test_catalog_drift_is_rejected() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2: a mutated inventory or a changed declaration leaves the comparison red.\n\n    Each case plants the fault the spec refutes with, on fixture data; the\n    first assertion is the counter-check that the comparator itself is green\n    on a clean render.\n    \"\"\"\n    alle = _fixture_gates()\n    rows = _rows(catalog_rows(alle))\n    assert _drift(alle, rows) == [], \"the clean render must pass its own comparison\"\n\n    assert _drift(alle, rows[:2]) == [\"missing row: probe-equivalent\"]\n\n    fremd = {**rows[0], \"id\": \"probe-foreign\"}\n    assert _drift(alle, [*rows, fremd]) == [\"extra row: probe-foreign\"]\n    assert _drift(alle, [*rows, rows[0]]) == [\"duplicate row: probe-command\"]\n\n    gelogen = {**rows[1], \"enforcement\": \"block\"}\n    assert _drift(alle, [rows[0], gelogen, rows[2]]) == [\n        \"probe-hosted: enforcement reads 'block', the gate declares 'advisory'\"\n    ]\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_gate_catalog.py",
          "reference": "test_catalog_drift_is_rejected",
          "start_line": 225,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false

          "citation": "tests/test_verify_cheap_first.py::test_local_blocking_failure_stops_before_pytest",
          "end_line": 453,
          "excerpt": "def test_local_blocking_failure_stops_before_pytest(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 3: a blocking seconds failure stops the local run before any minutes gate.\n\n    The list puts the minutes gate first; the cost order moves the failing\n    seconds gate ahead of it, its failure stops the run red, and the minutes\n    markers are never created.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = tmp_path / \"stop\"\n    gates = [\n        _gate(base, \"suite-minutes\", \"minutes\"),\n        _gate(base, \"quick-red\", \"seconds\", ending=\"echo 'a cheap diagnostic'; exit 1\"),\n        _gate(base, \"after-minutes\", \"minutes\"),\n    ]\n    tree = _tree_files(base / \"tree\")\n    _write_gate_file(tree, gates)\n    done = _run_runner(tree)\n    assert done.returncode == 1, f\"exit {done.returncode}\\n{done.stdout}\\n{done.stderr}\"\n    assert \"VERIFY RED\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    assert \"── [quick-red] RED (block)\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    assert (base / \"quick-red.ran\").exists()\n    assert not (base / \"suite-minutes.ran\").exists(), \"the expensive gate ran although a cheap gate had already failed\"\n    assert not (base / \"after-minutes.ran\").exists(), \"a gate after the blocking failure executed\"\n    # The cheap gate ran first: declaration order would have started the minutes gate.\n    assert (base / \"order.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"quick-red\\n\", done.stdout\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_verify_cheap_first.py",
          "reference": "test_local_blocking_failure_stops_before_pytest",
          "start_line": 430,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }

          "excerpt": "def test_new_change_creates_the_folder_and_a_current_index(workflow, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Acceptance of cke, first half: the entry scaffolds here.\n\n    The scaffold's stamp date is pinned: a `date` subclass overriding only\n    `today()` sits on the shared `datetime` module (`new_change.dt`), and the\n    assertion reads the pinned value directly — this module's\n    `from datetime import date` is import-bound and would keep reading the\n    calendar clock after the write.\n    \"\"\"\n    day = date(2026, 11, 10)\n\n    class PinnedDate(date):\n        @classmethod\n        def today(cls) -> date:\n            return day\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(new_change.dt, \"date\", PinnedDate)\n    exit_code = new_change.main([\"probe\", \"--bead\", OPEN_BEAD])\n    assert exit_code == 0\n    assert (workflow / \"changes\" / \"probe\" / \"research.md\").is_file()\n    assert reg.INDEX.is_file(), \"the index was not rendered along\"\n    # qd7: a new document is born current, or the check behind `frontmatter-current` would report it.\n    scaffold = (workflow / \"changes\" / \"probe\" / \"research.md\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert f\"\\nupdated: {day.isoformat()}\\n\" in scaffold.split(\"\\n---\\n\", 1)[0] + \"\\n\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def check(\n    name: str,\n    denylist: Path,\n    root: Path = REPO_ROOT,\n    prompt_texts: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n) -> Result:\n    \"\"\"Scan the scanned set under `root` against the denylist.\"\"\"\n    if not name or \"/\" in name or name in {\".\", \"..\"}:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no valid change name\",\n            \"Name the change folder under plans/changes/ (a single folder name). Without it the check cannot say what goes out.\",\n        )\n\n    rules, reason = read_denylist(denylist)\n    if reason is not None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no rule set to check against - the call does not start\",\n            f\"{reason}. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. What cannot be listed is not checked, and it would go into the call all the same.\",\n        )\n    result = Result(Verdict(), rules=len(rules), secret_rules=sum(rule.secret for rule in rules))\n    tree_files: list[Path] = []\n    link_texts: dict[str, str] = {}\n    unreadable = False\n    for part in listed.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").split(\"\\0\"):\n        if not part:\n            continue\n        path, name = root / part, part.rstrip(\"/\")\n        if path.is_file():\n            tree_files.append(path)\n        elif path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():\n            # Nothing stands behind the link, but the link's own text is what git shows of it.\n            link_texts[name] = str(path.readlink())\n        elif path.exists():\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{name} is listed by git but is not a regular file\",\n                \"A link to a directory, a submodule, a repository nested in the tree or a special file: a \"\n                \"reviewer reads through it and this check did not. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), path)\n\n    hits = 0\n    for relative, path in scanned.items():\n        try:\n            text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        except OSError:\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{relative} cannot be read\",\n                \"What cannot be read is not checked, and it goes into the call all the same.\",\n            )\n            continue\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict, exempt=_under_tests(relative, path))\n    for relative, text in link_texts.items():\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict)\n    if unreadable:\n        return result\n    result.files = len(scanned) + len(link_texts)\n\n    staged, why = _git(\n        root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--text\", \"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\", \"--no-renames\"\n    )\n    if staged is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the index cannot be read\",\n            f\"{why}. The index is what `git show :<path>` reads; skipping it would leave a staged value unchecked.\",\n        )\n    hits += _scan(\n        staged.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"),\n        \"staged changes (git diff --cached)\",\n      ",

          "excerpt": "def stamp(path: Path, today: date) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Set `updated:` to today by editing one line. True when the file changed.\n\n    Raises CannotStamp for a file that is not valid UTF-8: reading it with replacement\n    characters and writing it back would change bytes outside the line.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise CannotStamp(f\"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason} at byte {exc.start})\") from exc\n    ergebnis = stamped(text, today)\n    if ergebnis == text:\n        return False\n    path.write_bytes(ergebnis.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return True\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_frontmatter(text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse registry metadata from text, including YAML merge keys and aliases.\"\"\"\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\\n\"):\n        return None\n    end = text.find(\"\\n---\", 4)\n    if end == -1:\n        return None\n    try:\n        loaded = yaml.safe_load(text[4:end])\n    except yaml.YAMLError:\n        return None\n    return loaded if isinstance(loaded, dict) else None\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/plans_registry.py",
          "reference": "parse_frontmatter",
          "start_line": 62,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "The shared frontmatter parser in plans_registry silently degrades on unusual input: parse_frontmatter returns None when the text does not start with '---\\n', when no closing '---' is found, on a YAML error, or when the block parses to a non-dict — callers cannot distinguish 'no header' from 'malformed header'."
    },

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

      "House rule 9 in its sharpened form (one entry point and one writer, existing side routes folded in by their own change) bears on keeping a hand-edited header beside a renderer and on absorbing the per-question checks inside this change (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/6/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4).",
      "ADR 0009's 'No model as code in the kit now' reads, in its plain sense, as covering a typed relation schema. Its stated triggers do not match those the research names (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6).",
      "The online shared-model pattern comes from security and static-analysis tooling. Its transfer to repository gates is by analogy, with documented costs in extraction, slower checks, staleness, ripple across every consuming gate, and parser-specific escape hatches (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/9/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C5, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/9/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C5, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C3).",
      "No retrieved tool is shown to be a typed relation layer shared by repository gates. dependency-cruiser is adjacent: one validator with user-supplied rules (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/10/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/10/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C2).",
      "The retrieved failure records show reinterpretation across a serialised boundary and a parser/deserialization boundary, but none attributes a failure to gate checkers diverging from one shared model (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/11/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C5).",
      "A new blocking gate placed early in the cheap-first order hides every later gate in a local run, though CI still runs them (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4).",
      "Where the relation module lives decides whether it travels to instances: kit role and export rule are separate decisions (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4)."
    ],
    "architecture_comparison": "The documented architecture fixes one gate list (decisions/gates.yaml → ci_gates.py → verify_all.sh / generated ci.yml), with the gate file human-decided and every new gate tied to caller, kit, mutation and catalog ratchets (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7). The target architecture repeats 'one list' and requires every rule to name an enforcer (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5), and places the rule set in its H2 row, where it overlaps the proposed Rule model (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6). ADR 0009 rules out model-as-code in the kit for now and puts architectural deltas in design.md (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4). Two independent manifests decide kit role and export (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4). Against this, the research proposes typed models that mirror gates.yaml and provenance.yaml while those files stay the record. That is a second validator next to `validate_schema` (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3) and sits under house rules 8 and 9 (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4). A machine-checked rule-to-enforcer edge already exists in test_regelwerk (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6). How many scripts read provenance.yaml is disputed (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C5 against bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/2/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2). A full comparison is missing: the change has no design.md with an Architecture delta, the validate_change_artefacts.py presence gate named in WORKFLOW does not exist, and the tracker beads that would bound the change were not readable.",
    "assumptions": [
      "Several online claims describe page content that the runner excerpts do not show: the excerpts hold only titles and boilerplate.       "The claim that request smuggling is built on divergent parsers comes from the seat's background understanding, not from the excerpt text (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/11/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2).",
      "One claim reads research.md's 'voids a forty-minute run' as a configured limit, but the cited text describes the length of the voided run (16:28–17:11). A 40-minute finder limit appears only in seat counter-evidence prose and in an unpacketed commit (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/6/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4).",
      "The 'dozens of commits' with hand-accepted runner attempts is generalised from a ten-commit-per-path sample, and one of the hashes it names is not among its cited evidence (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/6/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7).",
      "Reader counts from greps (16 files under scripts/, fifteen test modules) count mentions, not verified readers (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/2/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/2/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5).",
      "That no spec, design or decisions file exists for this change rests on a folder listing, which is not a citable symbol (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5).",
      "That 0026 is the next free ADR number was measured only in the worktree's docs/adr. A superseded 0026 draft on another lane rests on a truncated handover excerpt (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C1).",
      "The class judgement holds 'architectural' as declared while noting that the research's own wording reads like a 'feature'. No repository rule decides between the two (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7).",
      "The red-run tests named for dangling-beads and decision-continuity are not among the cited symbols of the claim that names them (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/7/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4).",
      "The 'predominantly against stand-ins' judgement is bounded by the test files that seat opened (bb903f1132e2711d2a789c03072d2793/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7).",
      "That no packet commit adds a pydantic or Jinja2 import is weak evidence on its own, because the packet holds ten commits per path.
